access_tier.evidence_snippet: If you do not see the Admin section, contact your organization's admin or DealCloud Customer Success Manager (CSM) for assistance.

mcp.evidence_snippet: All DealCloud MCP tools are currently read-only and do not create, update, or delete data.

notes: Two auth paths: OAuth2 client_credentials (SDK + token endpoint, scope=publish for Publications) and a user-level API key enabled from Profile. MCP is read-only but REST is full CRUD, so buildability differs by path. Access is gated per-capability, not per-app: Publications requires separate account-manager enablement on top of the API capability. Schema Contracts exist because every site defines its own objects/fields/APINames, so one fixed toolkit cannot be shipped across tenants.

one_liner.value: Command-line tool that checks whether a username exists across hundreds of social sites
one_liner.evidence_snippet: Sherlock: Find Usernames Across Social Networks

api_surface.evidence_snippet: If you'd rather not install directly to your system, you can import the module at runtime with -m.

notes: Not a hosted service. Callable via sandboxed execution, not an API. No auth of its own; the real blocker is being blocked by the third-party sites it queries unauthenticated, which is why --tor and --proxy ship built in with a 60s default timeout. Output is text/CSV/XLSX files rather than structured stdout, so a wrapper must parse files. ToS consideration: this is account enumeration, which is a product decision as much as a technical one.

auth_methods.evidence_snippet: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN in a GitHub Actions workflow.

access_tier.evidence_snippet: If you want to use the GitHub REST API for personal use, you can create a personal access token.

api_surface.evidence_snippet: GitHub provides two APIs: a REST API and a GraphQL API.

notes: Multiple simultaneous auth paths: PAT (fine-grained or classic), GitHub App installation token, GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions, OAuth app token, and basic auth (client_id:client_secret) for a narrow set of app-management endpoints. Documents an explicit negative: username/password is not supported. SAML SSO orgs require separate token authorization for classic PATs, which is an org-level gate on top of self-serve credentials — a milder version of DealCloud's admin gating.
